name: The agent loop
summary: Plan, act with a tool, observe the result, and repeat until the goal is met.

D1.guide: Before you read: how would you know when a messy room is finished?
text: Think of a robot tidying a room: look around, pick one thing up, check where it goes, then look again. It keeps going until the room is tidy.
An AI agent works the same way, using computer tools instead of hands.
D1.analogy: A robot tidying a room, one item at a time.

text: The agent receives a goal. The model reasons about the next step and requests a tool call.
The harness runs the tool, with permission checks, and feeds the result back into the context.
The loop repeats until the model decides the task is done, a limit is reached, or a person steps in.
D2.analogyBreaks: A tidying robot can see the whole room. An agent only sees what's in its context, so long tasks need summaries and memory, and details can get lost.

predict.question: An agent keeps retrying the same failing command. Which safeguard matters most?
options: Step limits and human approval for risky actions
predict.explanation: Loops need stopping conditions and human checkpoints; otherwise errors repeat and costs grow.

text: Open problems: reliability over long tasks, knowing when to stop or ask for help, evaluating agents on realistic work, and containing agents that read untrusted content.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
